name: POST /api/leadflow/identity/links/:merge_id/retract - reverse a link, replay projections, verify the chain
description:
Retracts a verified identity link: emits the compensating event, replays the projections it invalidated, then asks sdk-audit whether the chain still verifies.

THE REASON IS MANDATORY HERE THOUGH UPSTREAM MAKES IT OPTIONAL. sdk-identity-resolver declares its unmerge body as { reason?: string }, so the platform will accept a retraction nobody explained. That is precisely the record an auditor needs most - somebody undid a link a steward had verified - so AC4 is enforced on this side rather than hoped for on the other.

NOTHING IS DELETED. unmergeRecords INSERTS a second merge_event with kind 'unmerge' and reverses_merge_id pointing at the original, which stays exactly where it was. An audit trail records that a thing was undone, not that it never happened, and a retraction that erased the link it reverses would destroy the evidence the link was ever made. The response states this as nothing_deleted rather than leaving it to be inferred.

THE REPLAY IS SCOPED TO THE SUBJECT, never the tenant. A tenant-wide replay to undo one link would rebuild every projection the tenant has - enormously more work, and enormously more blast radius than the retraction justifies.

THE CHAIN IS VERIFIED AFTER THE REPLAY AND REPORTED WHATEVER IT SAYS (AC3). A retraction that quietly broke the audit chain is worse than one that failed outright: the first leaves a tenant believing their trail is intact.

AN UNKNOWN MERGE ID ANSWERS 502, NOT 404, AND THAT IS UPSTREAM'S DOING. sdk-identity-resolver raises 'empi: merge <id> not found' into its 500 handler instead of answering 404, so a caller's bad id arrives here as a server error carrying callerFault:false. This definition states the 502 that actually happens rather than a 404 that never comes. It is deliberately NOT string-matched into a 404 on this side: inferring a caller fault from an upstream error message is how a genuine outage gets reported as a bad request. Raised for ProjexCloud to answer 404 instead.

requiresRole:["data_steward"] and NO testCase pins an Authorization header (MUST-71). QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: NEGATIVE: a retraction with no reason is refused, though upstream would accept it
NEGATIVE: an unknown merge id surfaces upstream's failure rather than a fabricated 404

payload.reason: Linked on a name variant that turned out to be two different people.

errorCases.message: reason is required to retract a link
errorCases.when: no reason accompanies the retraction. Enforced here BECAUSE upstream does not - its body declares reason optional, so the platform would record a reversal nobody explained.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the header is absent or not Bearer. Not authored as a testCase: pinning it would defeat the role swap (MUST-71).

errorCases.message: No policy grants this action to the caller's roles.
errorCases.when: the caller does not hold identity.merge_review. Not reachable while this definition runs under requiresRole.

errorCases.message: sdk-identity-resolver returned 500: empi: merge <id> not found
errorCases.when: the merge id does not exist, OR the resolver is genuinely unavailable. The two are INDISTINGUISHABLE from here because upstream answers 500 for an absent merge rather than 404 - see the description.
